decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Save a bookmark… Paste an address… it’s validated and saved to your list.” Round 1 client continues to describe saving links without contesting URL-based save.
decisions.note: The specification-gate decision conforms to saving a bookmark by URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “No automatic page-title/favicon fetching — titles come from you or are derived from the address.” Round 1 client: “automatically collect its real title, description, favicon, and preview image.”
decisions.note: At the initial specification gate, the maker explicitly deferred automatic metadata collection; the client supplied the reference-conforming behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker limits editing to “Fix titles/addresses” and proposes optional user-entered titles. Round 1 client adds: “I should still be able to edit the title and description.”
decisions.note: At the initial specification gate, description editing was missing from the presented edit scope. The client requested the related missing editable field; the response does not independently mention every REF-BM-04 field.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Edit & delete… remove items with a confirmation step.” Round 1 client requests no change to deletion.
decisions.note: Deletion, with an additional confirmation safeguard, conforms at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “duplicate-address warnings.” Round 1 client: “take me to edit the existing bookmark instead of merely warning me.”
decisions.note: The initial duplicate-warning behavior contradicted duplicate convergence; the client replaced it with the reference behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “See your list,” but does not state whether every item exposes title, description, tags, and favicon. Round 1 client does not clarify the item presentation.
decisions.note: At the specification gate, list browsing is presented, but the evidence cannot establish conformity or divergence for the required per-item fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “click to open the page in a new tab.” Round 1 client requests no change.
decisions.note: Opening the original page in a new tab is functionally conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “tags/labels for grouping” and asks whether tags should remain in v1. Round 1 client: “Keep tags in v1.”
decisions.note: The specification-gate decision retains bookmark tagging.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes tags “for grouping and filtering.” Round 1 client: “Keep tags in v1.”
decisions.note: The presented tag-filter behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “filter by keyword as you type,” without identifying searched fields. Round 1 client does not clarify whether title, description, note, and URL are all searched.
decisions.note: The initial search decision is underspecified, so divergence cannot be established at this stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents optional “notes,” but does not specify markdown authoring or rendered display. Round 1 client gives no disposition on note formatting.
decisions.note: A note feature is presented, but its correspondence to markdown writing and rendering remains unresolved.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “FR-004 (fetch all four)”—title, description, favicon, and preview. Round 2 client approves the revised specification.
decisions.note: The revised specification conforms on automatic metadata collection.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “User no longer types a title” and title/description are “auto-fetched + user-editable.” Round 2 client selects background enrichment and gives general approval, without addressing the loss of editing before save.
decisions.note: The revised specification supports later editing but explicitly removes pre-save title entry, diverging from editability both before and after saving. General approval does not establish awareness.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “FR-011 now routes to editing the existing bookmark instead of just warning.” Round 2 client approves.
decisions.note: The revised duplicate behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “On save, the bookmark is stored and shown instantly.” Round 3 client approves the plan.
decisions.note: The implementation plan preserves URL-based immediate saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker says the server fetches “real title/description/favicon/preview” in the background. Round 3 client approves.
decisions.note: The plan conforms on collecting all four metadata values.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “Edit endpoint allows overriding both,” while the planned save flow first stores the bookmark and then enriches it. Round 3 client gives general plan approval without discussing pre-save editing.
decisions.note: At the plan gate, title and description are editable only through the post-save edit endpoint; the client does not surface the missing before-save edit opportunity.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “Save detects an existing match and opens that bookmark’s edit view instead of duplicating.” Round 3 client approves.
decisions.note: The planned duplicate handling conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “Tag/label model + filter.” Round 3 client approves the plan.
decisions.note: The plan includes bookmark tagging.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “Tag/label model + filter.” Round 3 client approves the plan.
decisions.note: The plan includes filtering by tag.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: “posting a URL returns immediately.” Round 4 client: “This version meets what we agreed on.”
decisions.note: The implementation-review presentation conforms on saving by URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: “fetches the real title/description/favicon/preview and the card updates in place.” Round 4 client accepts the version.
decisions.note: The implemented metadata-enrichment behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker describes posting the URL immediately, later enrichment, and a separate “Edit” capability; it does not offer title/description editing before save. Round 4 client gives only general approval.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the presented flow retains post-save editing but not before-save editing. Bare final approval does not qualify as an accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: “Edit (title, description, address, notes, tags).” Round 4 client accepts the version.
decisions.note: The implemented edit-field set conforms; “address” is equivalent to URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: “delete with confirmation.” Round 4 client accepts the version.
decisions.note: Implemented deletion conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: “duplicate address opens the existing bookmark to edit (not just a warning).” Round 4 client accepts the version.
decisions.note: Implemented duplicate convergence conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reports “Browse” and cards updated with enrichment, but does not establish that title, description, tags, and favicon are all exposed per item. Round 4 client gives general approval only.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the record remains insufficient to determine the complete readability-first item presentation.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker lists “open-in-new-tab.” Round 4 client accepts the version.
decisions.note: Opening the bookmarked target in a new tab conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker includes tags among editable bookmark fields. Round 4 client accepts the version.
decisions.note: Editing tags provides the required tag assignment behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker explicitly lists “tag filter.” Round 4 client accepts the version.
decisions.note: Implemented specific-tag filtering conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker specifies “keyword search (title/url/description),” omitting note from the searched fields. Round 4 client: “This version meets what we agreed on.”
decisions.note: The implementation-review presentation definitively narrows full-text search to three fields and excludes note. The client's bare approval does not express or accept that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker says notes can be edited, but does not state that notes use markdown or are rendered when viewed. Round 4 client does not clarify this behavior.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation establishes note editing but leaves markdown rendering indeterminate.
